scope.method: Focused source and prior-owner screen of current held phrasal/set phrases outside A/B first 200 source-ordinal holds; not an exhaustive review of all holds. Excludes 4076 and previously rejected bespoke/transparent examples.

candidateRows.exactSourceSentence: Buses were pulling in throughout the morning.
candidateRows.sourceMeaning: Arriving and stopping, especially a vehicle; a natural phrasal verb.
candidateRows.currentHoldReason: Buses pulling in is literal arrival, not figurative idiom. Provisional editorial decision; independent review remains open.
candidateRows.sourceOwnerAssessment: The exact source has buses repeatedly pulling in, an established vehicle-arrives-and-stops phrasal sense; selected 2295 pull them in instead means attract an audience and selected 077 pull in the same direction means coordinate. The six-question lesson could contrast arrival, pass-by, departure and figurative attraction, but must avoid pretending pull in itself promises boarding or on-time service.
candidateRows.nextGate: Seven-step pilot with four-valid replies and source-distinct transport scenarios.

candidateRows.exactSourceSentence: Urban transport is not standing still.
candidateRows.sourceMeaning: Continuing to develop; a fixed motion idiom.
candidateRows.currentHoldReason: Not standing still means developing but overlaps standard make-progress patterns; course value needs review. Provisional editorial decision; independent review remains open.
candidateRows.sourceOwnerAssessment: The source applies not standing still to urban transport changing over time; a dictionary recognises stand still as stay the same and not change. Distinct from selected 3706 ahead of its time (premature innovation). The wording is simple and a seven-step lesson would need to test physical immobility versus continued development without repeating the same binary seven times.
candidateRows.nextGate: Course-value and seven-distinct-decision pilot before authoring.

notAdvanced.reason: The final puzzle piece literally slots into place in the exact source; a figurative lesson would require invented source sense.
Chairs discarded before their time personifies an idiom normally used for early death or premature events; do not teach a strained sense.
Automatic apology as a reflex is plausible but overlaps selected 1948 seamless reflex; owner-scope review before separate lesson.
